## Summary

I added two methods to the `Ledger` class in `ledger/entries.py`:

1. **`post_end_of_day(account, amount, day: date) -> Entry`** — Posts an entry at the last second (23:59:59 UTC) of the given date. This convenience method combines the date with a time object and delegates to the existing `post()` method. The timestamp is always UTC-aware per the active `timestamps-utc-aware` decision.

2. **`entries_since(since: datetime) -> list[Entry]`** — Returns all entries posted at or after the given datetime, sorted oldest first. This filters the ledger and returns results in chronological order.

Both methods respect the existing architecture:
- Timestamps are timezone-aware UTC datetimes (as required by the active decision)
- The implementation reuses the existing `post()` method, so end-of-day entries are indistinguishable from manually-posted ones
- All existing tests continue to pass
